options.name: arguments
options.description: Additional arguments provided on the command line that some init scripts accept.

options.name: daemonize
options.description: Have the module daemonize as the service itself might not do so properly. This is useful with badly written init scripts or daemons, which commonly manifests as the task hanging as it is still holding the tty or the service dying when the task is over as the connection closes the session.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the service should start on boot. At least one of O(state) and O(enabled) are required.

options.name: pattern
options.description: A substring to look for as would be found in the output of the I(ps) command as a stand-in for a status result. If the string is found, the service will be assumed to be running. This option is mainly for use with init scripts that don't support the C(status) option.

options.name: runlevels
options.description: The runlevels this script should be enabled/disabled from. Use this to override the defaults set by the package or init script itself.

options.name: sleep
options.description: If the service is being V(restarted) or V(reloaded) then sleep this many seconds between the stop and start command. This helps to workaround badly behaving services.

options.name: state
options.description: V(started)/V(stopped) are idempotent actions that will not run commands unless necessary. Not all init scripts support V(restarted) nor V(reloaded) natively, so these will both trigger a stop and start as needed.
